headline: This law makes it a federal crime to use or threaten force to block someone's religious practice, and it covers damage to religious buildings owned or leased by religiously affiliated nonprofits.
what_it_does: The law changes an existing federal crime that prohibits using force or threats of force to stop a person from freely practicing their religion. It says a threat of force includes a threat against religious property. It also creates a penalty of a fine, up to three years in prison, or both, when such an act damages religious property by more than $5,000. Finally, it expands the definition of religious real property to include property owned or leased by nonprofit groups with religious ties.

who_it_affects.group: Houses of worship and religious congregations
who_it_affects.how: Their buildings get stronger federal criminal protection against force, threats, and damage.
Property they own or lease, such as schools, charities, or community centers, is now covered as religious real property.

who_it_affects.group: People who damage or threaten religious property
who_it_affects.how: Such actions can now be prosecuted under federal law, with prison time up to three years if damage exceeds $5,000.
They have an added federal charge available for these offenses.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on September 28, 2018, and the summary does not give a separate effective date.
